Collection 
Review
By Carson Guise & Sofia Espinoza

Louis Vuitton
Pharrell Williams
1. Louis Vuitton began in 1837 when Louis Vuitton arrived in 
Paris, quickly becoming a valued craftsman at the Parisian 
atelier of Monsieur Maréchal for his trunk making
1. Pharrell has always had a passion for the arts, beginning 
in music and dance, transitioning to fashion over the past 
twenty years, making him the billionaire he is today
2. Louis Vuitton merged with Moët Hennessy in 1987 to 
create LVMH, of which it is a subsidiary. Moët et Chandon 
and Hennessy, leading manufacturers of champagne and 
cognac, merged respectively with Louis Vuitton to form 
the luxury goods conglomerate.
2. Vuitton and Pharrell first worked together in 2004. This 
was Williams first ever high fashion collaboration. Under 
the creative direction of Marc Jacobs, to make the 
“millionaire” golden decaled aviator sunglasses
3. Sells its product through standalone stores, leases in 
high-end department stores, and through the e-commerce 
section of its website
3. Pharrell believes in physical branding, always wearing 
statement pieces in public to show off his style. In 2005, 
he was known to have the most blinged-out pieces around 
anyone’s neck, with his chain weighing nearly a kilo
4. On 14 February 2023, Pharrell Williams was named 
creative director of men's wear for Louis Vuitton
4. William’s second collaboration with Louis Vuitton came 
about in 2008 when he designed jewelry for their “Blason” 
collection
5. Louis Vuitton brand really took off when Louis 
introduced his son, Georges Vuitton, to the production. 
Georges offered new ideas and products that had 
consumers begging for more, with innovations like the 
unpickable, multi-groove lock system 
5. Pharrell not only worked with Vuitton, but other high 
fashion brands like Chanel. Williams and Lagerfeld worked 
closely together to make the Chanel-Pharrell loafers

Strategy
Louis Vuitton’s strategy that they employ is a mixed strategy. 
While they are a luxury and high-end brand that offers creative 
and timeless pieces for large amounts of money, they make a 
lot of their revenue through their goodies. These goodies 
include things from keychains, to passport covers, to 
chocolates. They balance both their creative piece with these 
goodies, emphasizing the use of a mixed strategy. They have a 
strong brand identity which then results in strong consumer 
appeal.
Introducing Pharrell Williams as a creative director of Louis 
Vuitton runs the risk in terms of the consumer perception of 
the brand. Those who are very into fashion take credibility 
within fashion very seriously, and with William’s background in 
music. In the public’s eye, he devoting more time to music than 
he was to fashion. This presents a potential risk for Vuitton in 
terms of their credibility to their loyal fans of decades. With 
William’s new collection, the brand is gearing towards 
streetwear, something Vuitton is new to.

Hypothesis
Louis Vuitton has gone in the direction of streetwear 
recently to appeal to the younger generations that 
are beginning to become a large buying power in 
their business. Over the years, streetwear brands 
have taken fashion by storm, in some cases out 
performing even the top fashion houses. For 
example, the rise of the brands Bape and Supreme 
had young consumers in a “chokehold,” with some 
noting that you couldn’t even walk in a city without 
seeing someone wearing a pair. With the direction of 
Pharrell, Louis Vuitton is showing that they are ready 
to pivot into that market, emphasizing their 
adaptability to new trends to withstand their long 
standing brand name

Branding
In this collaboration, there is a lot at stake for both Louis 
Vuitton and Pharrell Williams. In this new era, they are running 
the risk of their brand reputation as they step into a more 
trend-focused designs. Louis Vuitton has always been known 
for being sleek, elegant, and professional and with these new 
collections they are branching away from their tried and true 
style, but keeping their branding consistent with the trunks and 
the iconic Louis Vuitton symbols. By the same token, their 
revenue is at stake in coalition with their brand reputation. They 
are taking a step completely away from what they are known to 
be, and this risk could cost them a lot of time and money.
In this collection there are a lot of striking looks that turned 
heads because of their creativity. Highlighted on the right are 
two looks that struck us as very different and unique to this 
collection. They push the boundaries of what Louis Vuitton is 
known for but do it in a way that is still high fashion. 
What Is New?

- Sleek and professional look
- LV brand symbol 
throughout the entire look
- Classic mary jane style 
loafer
- Homage to their past with 
classic monogram trunk
- Traditional suit jacket with 
a refreshed clean white look 
including silver accessories
- Trendy timeless necklaces  
- Iconic checkered LV 
monogram pattern
- Slightly flasher look with 
the monochrome outfit and 
pop of color 
- Shoes are accessible and 
styleable
- Sleek pieces with 
touches of the brands eye 
catching logo
- The LV belt is a timeless 
piece 
-Gives a new take on the 
classic suit and tie look 
with a fluffy monogram 
coat

Prada
1. This collection is contains majority of 
masculine presenting pieces, less fitted 
and baggier. Displayed in collared 
shirts, ties and blazers
1. This collection focuses on a more 
feminine figure, highlighting various 
aspects of women’s figures and being 
tighter to the body
-
Most of the collection’s tops 
look similar to blouses
2. The collection offers a variety of 
pants in different styles, only offering a 
small amount of shorts in comparison 
to Prada’s SS 2024 collection
2. There are far more looks within this 
collection utilizing shorts, highlighting 
its practicality for being a summer 
collection
3. Models are shown in many different 
styles of shoes creating appeal to 
many demographics. Shoes displayed 
include sneakers, high boots, loafers, 
slippers, low boots and many mary jane 
style clogs
3. Models are only shown wearing two 
types of shoes that are in various 
colors, representing the strict look that 
they are trying to maintain
